html:
Judaism is the religion of the Jewish people: belief in one God who made a covenant with Israel, and a way of life based on the Torah, the law given to Moses. It is one of the oldest living religions, and both Christianity and Islam grew from it.

It grew out of the religion of the kingdoms of Israel and Judah. When Babylon destroyed Jerusalem in 586 BCE and took its leaders into exile, the exiles held on to their identity through the law, the Sabbath and the writings that became the Hebrew Bible. After the return a Second Temple was built and stood for about six hundred years.

In the Roman period Judaism was divided into groups such as the Pharisees and Sadducees. From one Jewish movement came the followers of Jesus, whom Paul opened to non-Jews, the start of Christianity as a separate faith. When the Romans destroyed the Temple in 70 CE, sacrifice ended. The rabbis rebuilt the religion around study, prayer and the synagogue, and wrote down their teaching in the Mishnah around 200 CE and then the Talmud.

Jews lived across the Middle East, North Africa and Europe, as respected communities in some times and places and as persecuted minorities in others, as in the expulsion from Spain in 1492. Modern times brought new movements such as Hasidism and Reform Judaism, the Holocaust, and the founding of Israel in 1948.
